key.name: toggle-invert
key.description: Global keybinding that flips inversion on/off. Super+I by default; plain F5 is deliberately NOT used because a shell-level grab would shadow the browser's refresh shortcut. Change with gsettings: gsettings set org.gnome.shell.extensions.invertonator toggle-invert "['<Alt>i']"

key.name: toggle-pierce
key.summary: Toggle a true-color hole on the window under the pointer
key.description: Pierce analog of the Windows backend: the topmost window under the pointer stops being inverted (it is inverted a second time = double inversion = true color) while the rest of the screen stays inverted. Press again over the same window to close the hole; toggling inversion off clears every hole. NOTE: plain F7 is deliberately NOT the default — browsers claim F7 for caret browsing (Firefox/Chromium), and field testing on GNOME 51 showed an unmodified F7 grab does not consume the key. Super+F7 is browser-safe. Change with gsettings: gsettings set org.gnome.shell.extensions.invertonator toggle-pierce "['<Super>F7']"

key.name: auto-hole-media
key.description: While inversion is on, the focused window's AT-SPI2 tree is walked (budgeted, cached) and every image/video/animation element above 48px gets its own true-color rect hole — the rest of the screen stays inverted. Element rects beat the fullscreen auto-hole (fullscreen browser: video true, chrome inverted); windows whose tree proves no media keep the whole-window fullscreen hole as the fallback. Rects follow scrolling and tab switches. Requires AT-SPI2 (toolkit-accessibility is switched on automatically; GTK3 apps need a restart to pick it up). Opt out: gsettings set org.gnome.shell.extensions.invertonator auto-hole-media false

key.name: pin-hole
key.summary: Store a true-color area (select once, re-applied forever)
key.description: Opens a drag-select overlay: drag a rectangle over the area that should stay true color (e.g. the YouTube player), Esc cancels. The area is stored NORMALIZED to the focused window's frame, so it re-applies automatically whenever a matching window shows up — no tree walk needed, the hole is there the moment the window appears. Matching is title-first: the window title's stable segments are stored as tokens (a YouTube page always carries a "- YouTube" segment, video titles change and are matched loosely), falling back to the window class when the title carries nothing stable. Because the rect is stored relative to the window frame it follows moves and resizes; a matching window that goes FULLSCREEN drops the pin and lets the fullscreen auto-hole take over (the windowed player position is meaningless in fullscreen). Stored areas live in the pinned-holes key; manage them in the panel menu ("Stored areas"). Change with gsettings: gsettings set org.gnome.shell.extensions.invertonator pin-hole "['<Super>F8']"

key.name: pinned-holes
key.summary: Stored area pins (JSON, written by the pin feature)
key.description: JSON array of stored area pins, each: {"rel":[nx0,ny0,nx1,ny1], "cls":"wmclass", "tokens":["t1","t2"], "ts":epoch-ms}. rel is the rectangle normalized to the anchor window's frame rect (0..1); tokens are lowercase title segments a window must contain to match (title-first matching); cls is the fallback match on wm_class when no tokens could be derived. Edited via the panel menu (Super+F8 stores, the menu forgets); hand-editing works too but keep the JSON valid.

key.name: auto-hole-fullscreen
key.description: While inversion is on, any window that goes fullscreen is pierced automatically true-color — YouTube fullscreen, mpv, VLC, games. Leave it off to keep fullscreen windows inverted (opt out: gsettings set org.gnome.shell.extensions.invertonator auto-hole-fullscreen false). Manual Super+F7 holes are unaffected and are never auto-removed by un-fullscreening.

key.name: start-enabled
key.description: Written automatically on every toggle and re-applied on login, so the screen comes back inverted after a reboot if that is how you left it.
